messages:
jen-support: FYI customer TileCo hitting intermittent 429s during a short ingestion spike (approx 3k req/min for ~2m). They say their project API key shows plenty of quota and org billing is OK. They routed us curl logs with X-RateLimit headers and a NAT IP.
ben-sre: Can you paste the exact X-RateLimit* headers and whether requests went through a proxy/NAT? Any signs of multiple projects using same egress IP?
jen-support: Headers from one failing request: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 600000`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 451223`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 1720000000`. Egress IP: 34.120.12.9 (their CDN). Auth: `Authorization: Bearer org-token-xxxx` plus `x-api-key: sk-p-498-abc`. They also said other teams in their org flood concurrently.
sam-oncall: Tagging quota-bot and will pull attribution logs. At first glance this smells like NAT aggregation -> IP-based burst cap kicking in. @quota-bot can you dump the attribution for 34.120.12.9 around 3129876000-3129876600?
quota-bot: excerpt log:
```
request_id=rc-9a8b attr=project:p-498 org:o-22 api_key=sk-p-498-abc src_ip=34.120.12.9 status=429 reason=ip_burst_cap exceeded local_ip_rate=250 rps project_rate=0.8 rps
request_id=rc-9a8c attr=project:p-503 org:o-22 api_key=sk-p-503-xyz src_ip=34.120.12.9 status=200
request_id=rc-9a8d attr=project:p-498 org:o-22 api_key=sk-p-498-abc src_ip=34.120.12.9 status=200
```
quota-bot: summary: aggregated concurrent connections from 34.120.12.9 peaked at ~980 rps; we have an IP soft cap of 250 rps that is enforced when many distinct API keys map to same IP.
alice-platform: Quick note: our current scoping priority is "most restrictive wins" across (api_key/project, org, ip). Historically API key/project caps applied first, but we added IP affinity logic last quarter to prevent noisy neighbors from a single NAT. That can look surprising to customers who inspect only their key-level counters.
diane-support: TileCo also reported latency bump to ~800ms before 429s. Could be the rate limiter queueing requests then cutting flows.
ben-sre: Repro steps for internal triage and to send to the customer:
1) Simulate many clients behind same NAT: run `for i in {1..200}; do curl -H \"x-api-key: sk-p-498-abc\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer org-token-xxxx\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done` from one host (rate-limit will be IP aggregated).
2) Alternate keys across projects to show aggregation: `for k in keys.txt; do curl -H \"x-api-key: $k\" ... & done`
3) Check `ratelimit/attribution` logs with `jq` on request_id to confirm `reason=ip_burst_cap` or `reason=project_softlimit`.
Suggested mitigations to propose to TileCo:
- If you control egress, request a dedicated egress IP (Enterprise) or use Redwood Dedicated to avoid NAT aggregation.
- Stagger ingestion windows across projects or use a single coordinated API key with explicit per-project quotas.
- Apply a temporary org-level increase for the ingestion window; we can carve a burst allowance for the event.
ben-sre: Internally we'll consider telemetry improvements: surface `X-RateLimit-Reason` header with the enforcement tier (api_key/project/org/ip) to reduce confusion. Filing infra ticket.
sam-oncall: Action items: I will open infra ticket INF-4723 to evaluate raising IP soft cap thresholds for customers with known NATs, and to add clearer header reasons.
jen-support: I'll reply to TileCo with repro steps and these mitigations. Asking for sample pcap/evidence if they can share to prove all egress is from that single IP. Marking this thread P2. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
